intro: KM1-1's street props, buildings, set pieces and the tram, each built in high definition from your own views of it (front, right side, back, top and three-quarter, made in ChatGPT). Each is carved as one solid from its views' outlines, then textured from the views themselves: every point takes its pixels from the view that faces it squarely, can see it and shows the object there. Heights or widths are the real ones from the prompts; the rest comes from your views' proportions.

New in this round: the plain pole, the beige house, the little shrine and the station platform. The seventeen approved before are rendered again: joining halves and colouring hidden faces both changed this round, so the transformer pole's back and the street lamp's front come out a little different. A prop is about 1,450 triangles in a 1024 texture; the house 4,850, the shrine and the platform 3,880 each, and the tram 3,878, each in a 2048 texture. The board puts each beside your views: your front view and the model straight on at the same scale, your three-quarter view and the model at three-quarters, then the model from the street.
fixed: Found and fixed while building this round (D27): the platform's two halves joined with a grey strip and a doubled post. Each half ends in a grey margin past its cut, so halves now join where their objects overlap. The views of one object must also come out the same size, which straightened the transformer pole's back (3 % too tall before) and the lamp's front. The shrine's back is drawn narrower than its front and left grey on the model; now a view only colours what it shows. The house's balcony, door canopy and window hood ran the whole width of its front as thin ledges; now they stand out only where they are. A tunnel through the platform's back wall, which only its front view drew, is closed. The house and the platform now build in minutes instead of 40.

From earlier rounds (D25, D26): the pole's spikes and grey slabs, square posts, grey on the backs, open edges, the red machine's notch, the air conditioner's shelf and the signal's guard frame (open now).
limits: The little shrine: its views disagree. The side view shows the steps standing out in front of the walls; the front, top and three-quarter views show walls beside them. So its walls are carved from the front and top alone, and its lantern is set to its own depth. Its back is drawn a quarter narrower than its front, so its back's edges take its sides' pixels. Faces no view sees take the stones of the nearest side. Its left side copies its right, lantern included.

The station platform is 7.6 m long at its 3.2 m height: your views' proportions, where the prompt said 10 m. Its gateway shows the back wall behind it, since only its front view drew a passage through.
The tram's roof units: its BACK draws them where its FRONT and TOP have them, not mirrored, so their far faces take the roof's pixels. Only the far side shows it.
The ticket gate: its flap is a thin plate set by hand, and its top takes the nearest sides' pixels; its views disagree about the flap.
Sides with no view of their own take the opposite side's pixels: every model's left side takes its right side's.
Thin parts (poles' bolts and cables, the bicycle's spokes and basket mesh) are in the texture, not the solid; the bicycle's spokes are cut out.
pending: Next from you: the wire gantry (KM-B07) again, one image a view: its halves came at two scales. Its prompt's ChatGPT line now asks for that.

In the game: the seventeen approved are in the project (Assets/_Game/Art/Models/Kamakura). The plain pole, the house, the shrine and the platform go in once you approve them, with the seventeen as rendered here. Then KM1-1 places them.
